newsitem.title: FRANCE: GAN expected to sell off more real estate.
newsitem.headline: GAN expected to sell off more real estate.

text.p: French state-owned insurer GAN, gearing up for privatisation later this year, will open tenders this week for nearly four billion francs worth of distressed property, an industry source said on Monday.
"We have completed the study phase and we will start with the tender procedure. We will start this week. It will take some time. We are working toward the autumn," said the source.
The property, bought when the French real estate market was at its peak, has a gross value of 16.9 billion francs and a net value of 3.8 billion francs after 13.1 billion francs of provisions.
GAN said a feasibility study by U.S. bank Bankers Trust New York Corp would be ready in several weeks, though no decision has been made on whether the sale will go ahead .

The assets, mainly buildings in the Paris area, have been put in Baticredit and Parixel, two special companies designed to hold distressed property which were set up when GAN's property woes threatened to engulf the insurer.
GAN is the latest in a series of French financial institutions seeking to unload property whose value has plunged as much as 70 percent since the property bubble burst in mid-1990.

So far the main buyers for distressed French real estate have been so-called U.S. vulture investors, which earned billions of dollars in the early 1990s by snapping up unwanted U.S. real estate, and hope to replicate their success in Europe.

Late last year, Credisuez, set up by Cie de Suez to manage a property empire which was at one time worth 19.7 billion, francs sold property development activities to Goldman Sachs Whitehall Street fund for three billion, a billion below its book value.
Property specialists said that what sets the GAN sale apart is that it involved buildings rather than property loans which take a long time to recover.
"This tender should draw a more diversified group of clients, not just Americans but also Europeans and perhaps French," said one property specialist.
GAN, which sold 1.8 billion francs of property in 1996, said earlier this year it plans to sell all the rest in the coming months.
The spokesman said the sale of the assets would help clear the decks for GAN's privatisation by clarifying the situation.

Moves to privatise GAN have been put on hold by the two- round parliamentary election to be held on May 25 and June 1. But if polls pointing to re-election of the ruling centre-right coalition are correct, the sale is expected to go ahead before the end of the year.
